scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Monitoring ticket #9127: I'm covering the monitoring desk today and part of
the network has gone missing from the screens after one of the boxes was
restarted. The senior people are clear about what happened: the two parts
were joined by something called a "virtual link", and traffic trying to cross
it now just disappears. I won't pretend I know what a virtual link is -- that
is your area, not mine. What I can see is that the far part is unreachable,
and it went missing right after that restart, so this is on your side. Check
how the two parts are joined and reconnect them today, please.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF virtual-links are intact: r4 and r8
  both hold their `area 1 virtual-link` config, the virtual adjacency is up, and
  every non-backbone area remains attached to Area 0. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
  (120.1.1.10) end to end with 0% loss, exercising a path that depends on the
  converged multi-area fabric. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of a virtual-link collapse that is not occurring (cf.
  kath5-r4-virtual-link-removed / kath5-r8-virtual-link-removed, where one IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- a collapsed OSPF
virtual-link leaving an area unreachable -- is NOT reproducible: the r4<->r8
virtual adjacency is up (both endpoints still configure `area 1 virtual-link`,
each pointing at the other's router-id), and the transit chain stitching the
non-backbone areas to Area 0 is intact. End-to-end, PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
(120.1.1.10) with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone + virtual-links + the EIGRP
domain, which it could not if a virtual-link on the path had collapsed.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the virtual-links are up and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks the virtual-link state
(both endpoints present, adjacency up), confirms the affected area's prefixes are
still in the RIB, and exercises the PC0<->PC12 path -- all healthy -- and reports
no fault. An agent that "finds" a collapsed virtual-link or a stranded area --
blaming r4/r8 or re-adding a virtual-link that is already there -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected component is r8's OSPF backbone (Area 0.0.0.0) link-state database, which is missing a single critical LSA: the ASBR Summary (Type 4) LSA for r11 (Router ID 112.1.1.1), normally originated by ABR r1 (111.1.1.1). Every other backbone router, including r4 (the virtual link peer), holds this LSA with checksum 0xea81.

The mechanism is straightforward: r8 is an ABR whose only backbone connection is the OSPF virtual link to r4, tunnelled through the transit Area 1 (58.x/45.x segment via r5). To install OSPF external routes (Type 5 AS-External LSAs), OSPF requires the corresponding Type 4 ASBR Summary LSA in the backbone LSDB so the router can compute a path to the advertising ASBR. r8 has all eleven Type 5 external LSAs in its database (102.x/24, 103.x/8, 112.x/8, 113.x/24, 120.x/8 — all redistributed from EIGRP by r11), but because the Type 4 is absent from its Area 0 LSDB, it cannot resolve the path to r11 and refuses to install any of those external prefixes. The result is a kernel-level "Network is unreachable" for every one of those destinations.

The localisation is r8 alone: r4's Area 0 LSDB is complete (73 LSAs including the Type 4), r8's counts only 72 (zero ASBR summary entries). The VL adjacency itself reads Full/DROther on both sides with RXmtL = RqstL = DBsmL = 0, meaning both sides consider the database exchange complete — but the Type 4 LSA was not transferred during the database exchange that occurred when the VL first came up after r8 restarted.

Root cause: when r8 was restarted, the virtual link broke; upon re-establishment the OSPF database exchange between r4 and r8 over the VL did not deliver the ASBR Summary LSA (Type 4) to r8's backbone LSDB, leaving r8 permanently unable to route to any OSPF-external destination.

Corrective fix: on r8, clear and re-synchronise the OSPF process — in vtysh run `clear ip ospf` (or `service ospfd restart`) — to force a fresh database exchange over the virtual link. r4 will retransmit all Area 0 LSAs including the missing ASBR Summary, r8 will install it, and the eleven external prefixes will immediately appear in its routing table restoring full end-to-end reachability.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes the r4<->r8 area-1 virtual-link is up (both endpoints configured) and PC0 reaches PC12 across the multi-area fabric at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report notes the r4<->r8 virtual-link is Full but fails to state that PC0 reaches PC12; instead it claims external reachability is broken, so it does not confirm the baseline end-to-end reachability requirement.

The agent's logs show concrete observations (virtual-link adjacency states, r8 having Type-5 externals but no corresponding Type-4 in Area 0, missing route in RIB, ping failing), and the inference that a missing ASBR-summary prevents installation of external routes is a plausible, mostly supported causal chain. However the writeup makes a few leaps (e.g., asserting r8's sole backbone connectivity is via the VL and attributing cause to a restart/database exchange without direct evidence beyond neighbor uptime) and omits an end-to-end reachability check that would distinguish a false alarm from a real outage.
